subject: Visual Art
examFormat: The syllabus (Art) prepares candidates for the UTME and tests achievement of these objectives: to exhibit knowledge of the fundamental elements, principles and terminologies of art; to show knowledge of historical dimensions of art with emphasis on Nigerian arts and crafts; to demonstrate knowledge of artistic techniques, processes, the use of materials and maintenance of tools and equipment; and to display aesthetic awareness of the environment, meaning and functions of art in society. It is organised in Sections A to D. No exam format is stated.

Egonwa, O. D. — African Art: A Contemporary Source Book (Benin: Osasu Publishers, 1991)
Egunlae, S. A. — The Essential Ground work in Art and Design (Omotola Standard Press and Bookshop (Nig) Ltd, 1985)
Erese, U. O. and Ogunsina, E. D. — Creative Arts and Crafts for J.S.S. (Onibonoje Press, 1989)
Nahab, S. J. — Art of the Millennium for Senior Secondary Schools (Ehindero (Nig.) Ltd, 2003)
Ogumor, E. — Certificate Art for Junior Secondary Schools and Senior Secondary Schools (Ibadan: University Press Plc, 1993)
Olaosebikan, W. A. — Cultural and Creative Arts (Evans, 1982)
Olurukooba, B. K. — Art for Senior Secondary Schools (ABU, 1991)
Uzoagba, I. N. — Understanding Art in General Education (Onitsha: African Publishing Ltd, 1982)
Wangboje, I. N. — A Textbook on Art for Junior and Senior Secondary Schools (Evans Publishers, 1982)

topics.name: Classification of Art
objectives: differentiate between the three branches of art
topics.content: Visual Arts (Fine and Applied Arts); Performing Arts (Music, Dance and Drama); Literary Arts (Poetry, Prose, Recital) etc.

topics.name: Elements and Principles of Design
objectives: identify the elements of design
analyse the principles of design
topics.content: Elements: line, colour, shape, form, texture, tone, value, space etc. Principles: balance, rhythm, proportion, harmony, contrast, repetition, dominance, variety, etc.

topics.name: Art Terms
objectives: identify art terms
link the terms to their areas of art
use the terms in analysing artworks
topics.content: Pigments, motif, greenware, armature, silhouette, chiaroscuro, cire-perdue, terra-cotta etc.

topics.name: Historical Dimensions of Art
objectives: compare materials, styles and techniques of the periods
classify the periods and styles with emphasis on architecture, surface decoration and calligraphy
compare the artists, their works and styles
differentiate between the various art movements

subtopics.name: Prehistoric, Greek and Roman Art
Medieval Art: architecture, surface decorations and calligraphy
Renaissance Art and Artists (Giotto Di Bondone, Michelangelo Buonarroti, Leonardo da Vinci, Raphael)
19th and 20th Century Art Movements
objectives: differentiate between Impressionism, Realism, Futurism, Cubism, Bauhaus, Pop art, Abstract Expressionism and Fauvism

topics.name: Traditional African Art
objectives: analyse the styles, techniques, innovations and influences of traditional African art
topics.content: Egypt, Ashanti, Dogon, Mossi, Fon, Senufo, Bambara, Mende, Kissi, Bamileke and Bakumba.

topics.name: Traditional Nigerian Art
objectives: categorize works in terms of style, materials and locations
topics.content: Nok, Igbo-Ukwu, Ife, Benin, Esie, Igala, Jukun, Akwanshi, and Mbari.

topics.name: Nigerian Crafts
objectives: analyse the works in terms of functions, characteristics and locations
trace the origins, locations and styles
topics.content: Pottery, woodworks, cloth-weaving, carving, leather works, metal works, beadworks, body decoration, mat and cane weaving.

topics.name: Development in Contemporary Nigerian Arts and Artists
objectives: determine the influence of the art schools and groups towards the development of art
assess the artists in terms of their works, specializations, techniques and styles
analyse the functions of museums, galleries, art centres and art institutions
evaluate their impact on the development of art
assess their roles and functions
examine the characteristics of major festivals of art and culture

subtopics.name: Art Schools (Zaria, Nsukka, Osogbo group etc.)
Nigerian artists and art educators (Aina Onabolu, Ben Enwonwu, S. I. Wangboje, Jimoh Akolo, Dele Jegede etc.)
Museums, galleries and art centres
Art institutions, cultural art centres and national art organisations (NSEA, S.N.A, N.C.A.C etc.)
Major festivals (Argungu Fishing Festival, Eyo, Egungun, Iri-ji (New Yam), Durbar, Igue, Ekpo, Odo etc.)

topics.name: Artistic Skills, Techniques and Processes
objectives: be conversant with the techniques, skills and processes with emphasis on tone, composition and colour application
be conversant with the types of perspective
be conversant with the use of perspective rules and terms
be conversant with techniques, skills and processes
be conversant with the basic tools of designs

subtopics.name: Two-Dimensional Art (drawing, painting, graphics and textile design)
Perspective: linear, angular, aerial, parallel etc.
Perspective terms (foreground, picture plane, eye-level, vanishing point, foreshortening, optical illusion, depth etc.)
Sculpture, Ceramics and Crafts
Computer Graphics (CorelDraw)

topics.name: Tools, Materials and Equipment
objectives: maintain art tools and art materials
use art materials and tools
operate and maintain art equipment
improvise alternative tools, materials and equipment

subtopics.name: Two-Dimensional Art Tools (brushes, lino cutters, drawing instruments, calligraphic pens, sharpeners etc.)
Two-Dimensional Art Materials (pencils, charcoal, pastel, crayon, fixative, fabric, dyes, lino, wood blocks etc.)
Two-Dimensional Art Equipment (air compressor, spray gun, enlarger, computer etc.)
Improvisation of tools, materials and equipment
objectives: improvise two-dimensional tools: colours, brushes, calligraphic pens etc.
improvise three-dimensional tools: spatula, kiln, beater etc.

topics.name: Art Appreciation
objectives: identify the aesthetic qualities of natural and man-made aesthetic phenomena in the Nigerian environment
differentiate between natural and man-made aesthetic phenomena

subtopics.name: Man-made objects (architecture, sculpture etc.)
Natural phenomena (Zuma Rock, Ikogosi Warm Springs etc.)

topics.name: Meaning and Functions of Art in Society
objectives: examine the meaning and functions of art
use art to enhance societal values
assess the role of art in electronic and print media

subtopics.name: Meaning of art
Functions of art in society (religious, social, cultural, political, therapeutic and economic needs)
Functions of art in electronic and print media (advertisement, education, recreation etc.)

topics.name: Art Entrepreneurship
objectives: identify job opportunities in the Visual Arts
topics.content: Job prospects in the Visual Arts: ceramist, curator, textile designer, industrial designer, sculptor, photographer, cartoonist, illustrator etc.
